 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.443/2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 25/09/2019.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 30/03/2018 at about 09:45 a.m., while he was walking through the western side of the Elanthikkara-Madathumpady road and when he reached the place by name Keezhupadom, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-41/A-3211 ridden by the second respondent in a rash and 2025:KER:59269 MACA NO. 466 OF 2020 negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 8,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied negligence on the part of the second respondent.
The age, occupation, income etc., of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A13 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the third respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part 2025:KER:59269 MACA NO. 466 OF 2020 of the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,41,700/-
together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal as 10,000/- is quite low in the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

2 2020 the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income is fixed as 11,500/- per month.

sentences.text: Loss of earnings 10.

The materials on record show that following injuries were sustained by the claim petitioner:
"1) fracture of distal tibia and fibula (right)
2) fracture of proximal left tibia 3) fracture of right fifth metacarpal base etc."
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 21 days.
Hence, in these circumstances, in all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 8 months.

Therefore, I find that he can be granted compensation towards loss of earnings for a period of 8 months, that is, 92,000/-
(11,500 x 8 months).
Percentage of permanent disability 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that as per Ext.A10 disability certificate, when the disability has been assessed as 30.07%, the Tribunal was totally unjustified in scaling down the disability to 10%.

The claim 2025:KER:59269 MACA NO. 466 OF 2020 petitioner being a labourer, the injuries sustained had certainly affected his earning power and therefore the percentage of disability fixed is quite low and hence the same needs to be rectified.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that Ext.A10 certificate was not issued by a medical board and that it has been issued by a private doctor and hence, the marking was objected.

As the contents of the document has not been proved, the same cannot be relied on,
goes the argument.
11.1. The marking of Ext.A10
was objected on behalf of the third respondent/insurer before the Tribunal.
The doctor who issued the certificate was also not examined to prove its contents.
Admittedly, the certificate has not been issued by a Medical Board or by a Government doctor.
It has been issued by a private doctor.
That being so, I find that the Tribunal was justified in not relying on Ext.A10.
However, the fact that the accident occurred and that the claim petitioner sustained the aforesaid injuries is not disputed.

Taking into account the avocation of the claim petitioner and the injuries sustained by him, which include fractures on both legs, I find that fixing the percentage of disability as 15%, in the absence of any better evidence, would be reasonable.
Loss of amenities in life 12.
Though an amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal granted an amount of 30,000/- only, which is also stated to be on the lower side.
In the light of the injuries sustained and the period of hospitalization, I find that an amount of 50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
